title: Cofinal-tail continuity of Hom between perfect complexes
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preordered set, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram with colimit cocone $c$ and colimit ring $A$, $i\in I$, and $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme]. Assume the scheme derived categories and the derived categories on the localized open sites of X exist [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $P,Q\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Use the schemes, direct pullbacks and canonical conjugated Hom transport $T$ of [lem-pc-perfect-hom-transport]. Then (1) for every $j_0\ge i$ and every $\varphi:P_\infty\to Q_\infty$ there are $j\ge j_0$ and $a:P_j\to Q_j$ such that $T_{j,\infty}(a)=\varphi$; (2) whenever $a,b:P_j\to Q_j$ have equal images under $T_{j,\infty}$, there exists $k\ge j$ such that $T_{j,l}(a)=T_{j,l}(b)$ for every $l\ge k$. This statement does not assert descent of inverses or simultaneous satisfaction of a finite set of relations.

proof.text: Affine case. Let U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i) be affine, U_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j) and U=\operatorname{Spec}(A) its preimages, A=\operatorname{colim}_jA_j (affine transition morphisms). P_i|_{U_i} and Q_i|_{U_i}[n] are perfect, hence in D_{QCoh} (Tag 08DB, as in Step 1), so by [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] they are isomorphic to \widetilde{E_0} and \widetilde{K_0} for bounded complexes E_0, K_0 of finite projective A_i-modules; K_0, a bounded complex of flat modules, is K-flat (Stacks Tag 0649). Since the terms are flat, the derived pullbacks to U_j and U are \widetilde{E_0\otimes_{A_i}A_j}, \widetilde{K_0\otimes_{A_i}A_j} and \widetilde{E_0\otimes_{A_i}A}, \widetilde{K_0\otimes_{A_i}A}. The equivalence D(A)\simeq D_{QCoh}(O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}) [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] (D_{QCoh} being a full subcategory) identifies the Hom sets in D(O_{U_j}) and D(O_U) with those in D(A_j) and D(A), compatibly with the transition maps, and the affine calculation [lem-pc-affine-perfect-hom-colimit] then gives the bijection \mathcal P(U_i).

source.place: Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine case in the proof

proof.text: The assertion is local on the finitely presented scheme X_i. For a quasi-compact open U_i of X_i with preimages U_j in X_j and U in X, let \mathcal P(U_i) be the condition that for every integer n the canonical map \operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(O_{U_j})}(P_j|_{U_j},Q_j|_{U_j}[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(O_U)}(P|_U,Q|_U[n]) is bijective. Since X_i is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, it suffices by the induction principle for quasi-compact opens [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] to prove \mathcal P for affine opens (Step 1) and the gluing step. For the gluing step let W=U\cup V with U quasi-compact, V affine, and \mathcal P holding for U, V, U\cap V. A perfect object lies in D_{QCoh} (it is locally strictly perfect with quasi-coherent terms [def-pc-perfect-complex]; Stacks Tag 08DB), so the derived Mayer–Vietoris triangle [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle] applies to Q_j|_{W_j} on each W_j and to Q|_W on the preimage of W. Applying \operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{W_j},-[n]) and identifying \operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{W_j},R(j_U)_*Q_j|_{U_j}[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{U_j},Q_j|_{U_j}[n]) by the adjunction L j_U^*\dashv R(j_U)_* for the open immersion (where L j_U^* is restriction) [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint], and likewise for V and U\cap V, gives the long exact Mayer–Vietoris Hom sequence at each stage j and on the preimage of W; these sequences are compatible with derived pullback because pullback commutes with restriction to opens. Filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact, so the colimit of the stage sequences is exact, and the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma], applied around the term for W in degree n (whose four neighbours are terms for U, V, U\cap V in degrees n-1 and n, bijective by hypothesis), shows \mathcal P(W). The case W=X_i is the required bijection.

proof.text: The n=0 comparison bijection is unchanged on each cofinal tail above a fixed j0, so it supplies a representative at j at least j0. The filtered-set colimit equality criterion turns equality of two limit images into equality at some later k. Every further transition preserves that equality by functoriality, giving the whole tail. The comparisons and transition maps are compatible by the composition coherence node.
